digital-signal-processing--dft.title: DFT as the DTFT sampled at N points
digital-signal-processing--dft.note: The DFT is not a different transform: it is the DTFT evaluated on the grid 2 pi k / N, so one period of the DTFT holds all N bins.

digital-signal-processing--fft.title: Recursive radix-2 FFT
lines: tw = [cmath.exp(-2j * cmath.pi * k / n) * odd[k] for k in range(n // 2)]
return ([even[k] + tw[k] for k in range(n // 2)] +
digital-signal-processing--fft.note: Splitting into even and odd inputs gives two half-length transforms; the twiddle multiply and the plus/minus pair are one butterfly per stage.

digital-signal-processing--window-functi.title: Window trade-offs for length N
digital-signal-processing--window-functi.note: A wider main lobe buys lower side lobes: every window trades transition width against stopband attenuation, and the rectangular one loses on both.

digital-signal-processing--butterworth-f.title: Filter order from the attenuation spec
digital-signal-processing--butterworth-f.note: Dividing the two spec equations cancels the unknown cutoff, leaving a closed form for the smallest integer order that meets both edges.

digital-signal-processing--bilinear-tran.title: Where the tangent warping comes from
digital-signal-processing--bilinear-tran.note: On the unit circle the map is purely imaginary, and the tangent squeezes the infinite analog axis into the interval between minus pi and pi.

digital-signal-processing--impulse-invar.title: Analog-to-digital mapping methods
rows: no aliasing, poor at high Ω
z = e^(sT) for each pole and zero
no aliasing, keeps the pole map
digital-signal-processing--impulse-invar.note: Only the bilinear map folds the whole left half-plane one-to-one inside the unit circle, at the price of frequency warping.

digital-signal-processing--overlap-add.title: Overlap-add vs overlap-save
digital-signal-processing--overlap-add.note: Both turn one long convolution into circular FFT blocks; they differ only in whether the wrap-around part is added back or thrown away.

digital-signal-processing--linear-phase-.title: Symmetry gives exactly linear phase
steps: \text{pair }n\text{ with }N-1-n:\quad e^{-j\omega m}+e^{j\omega m}=2\cos\omega m\ \text{is real}
digital-signal-processing--linear-phase-.note: Symmetric coefficients make the bracketed sum real, so the entire phase is the pure delay of (N-1)/2 samples.
